title: Docket is sequential by docket number; citations must be verified
issue_presented: How must Atlas agents treat Governance V2 docket order, timestamps, and any cited docket number?

known_facts.fact: The human Viewer Docket is ordered by sequential docket number (Dkt. 1, 2, 3, …). Each row’s timestamp is that entry’s filed_utc, which must not contradict that number order.
User instruction 2026-08-23: the Docket must run by docket numbers with matching timestamps, and any AI reference to a docket number must be double-checked.
J-0011: the Viewer and its INDEX.json are a lens, not a second source of law. The index is not authoritative if it disagrees with a canonical artifact hash.

analysis: Sorting the Docket by document date or title groups later refilings next to earlier numbers and makes a guessed Dkt. N unsafe. Agents must not invent or reuse a docket number from chat, memory, a PDF filename, or a prior message without reading the current index (and, if citing substance, the canonical source path on that entry).
judgment_rule: The Governance V2 Docket is ordered by sequential docket number with no gaps: Dkt. 1, 2, 3, … through N. Display and citation order is that sequence — not document date, title, or type.
The timestamp shown for a docket row is that entry’s filed_utc. Along increasing docket numbers, timestamps must be non-decreasing. A later docket number is a later (or same-second) entry.

A new filing receives the next sequential docket number and a new filed_utc at the moment it is docketed. A later change to a canonical artifact is a new filing (new number, new timestamp); the prior filing and its PDF are preserved.

If numbers have gaps, duplicates, or timestamps that do not match docket order, redocketing is authorized: keep each entry’s original filed_utc, sort by that timestamp, reassign Dkt. 1..N, and rename filed PDFs to the new numbers. Do not rewrite canonical artifacts. Record prior_docket_nos. After a redocket, every docket-number citation must be verified again.

Any agent reference to a docket number (Dkt. N, docket_no, a Dkt-NNNN PDF name, or equivalent) must be double-checked against the current viewer/docket/INDEX.json (or the live Viewer Docket) before it is treated as KNOWN. Do not cite a docket number from memory, a previous chat, or an inferred grouping.

A verified citation states: docket_no, filed_utc, artifact_id, and source_path from that index row. If the index row’s source_hash disagrees with the canonical file, flag a discrepancy and do not silently prefer the index (J-0011).
If the number cannot be verified, label the citation UNKNOWN or USER_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED. Do not invent a docket number to fill a gap — redocket instead, then cite the new verified number.
This Judgment does not make INDEX.json current law. Canonical artifacts remain outside viewer/. The Viewer remains read-only as to canonical Governance state.
operational_effect: STARTUP.md and Viewer onboarding require this check. Agents loading J-0011 also load J-0013 before using docket numbers in Findings, Jobs, Orders, or user-facing text.
exceptions: Historical public Atlas-Governance cabinet docket numbers (DKT-NNNN papers) are a different series. They remain historical evidence and must not be treated as Governance V2 Viewer docket numbers without an explicit mapping that has been verified.
required_validation: Viewer Docket lists entries in docket_no order; filed_utc is non-decreasing along that order; agent citations to Dkt. N are checked against INDEX.json.
